root_cause.text: The adxl380 IIO interrupt handler incorrectly assumed the FIFO entry count from the hardware would align with `st->fifo_set_size` scan batches, so it iterated in enabled-channel-sized chunks even though the device FIFO is populated one sample at a time, causing reads past the actual FIFO contents when the count was not a multiple of that batch size.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states “the sensor fills the FIFO one sample at a time, even when more than one channel is enabled” and that “the number of entries reported by the FIFO status registers may not be a multiple of N,” while the fix adds `fifo_entries = rounddown(fifo_entries, st->fifo_set_size);` immediately before the loop `for (i = 0; i < fifo_entries; i += st->fifo_set_size)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Round down FIFO entry count to full set-size units before reading so the IRQ handler only processes complete FIFO samples.
intent_record.what: A new statement was added in adxl380_irq_handler() that assigns fifo_entries = rounddown(fifo_entries, st->fifo_set_size); immediately before the loop that reads FIFO data in increments of st->fifo_set_size.
intent_record.how: This ensures the number of FIFO entries processed is rounded down to a whole multiple of the configured FIFO set size, preventing the loop from attempting a final partial read and keeping FIFO reads aligned to complete sample sets.

grouping_result.intent: Round down FIFO entry count to full set-size units before reading so the IRQ handler only processes complete FIFO samples.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adjusting the FIFO entry count to only full set-size batches before the IRQ handler reads data, preventing processing/readout beyond actual FIFO contents when the hardware count is not a multiple of st->fifo_set_size.

candidates.rationale: This loop assumes fifo_entries is divisible by st->fifo_set_size and processes FIFO data in scan-sized chunks. When the hardware FIFO count is not a multiple of the enabled-channel batch size, the loop still advances in set-size steps and drives reads for incomplete trailing samples, leading to reading past the actual FIFO contents.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop uses the raw hardware FIFO entry count as the termination condition while incrementing by st->fifo_set_size, implicitly assuming the FIFO count is aligned to enabled-channel scan batches. Because the device FIFO is filled one sample at a time, a non-multiple trailing count causes the handler to iterate as if a full batch exists and read past valid FIFO contents.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `adxl380_irq_handler()`, so the snippet is sufficient. After reading the hardware FIFO count with `adxl380_get_fifo_entries(st, &fifo_entries);`, the handler loops as `for (i = 0; i < fifo_entries; i += st->fifo_set_size)`. Inside that loop it performs `regmap_noinc_read(..., &st->fifo_buf[i], 2 * st->fifo_set_size);` and then `iio_push_to_buffers(indio_dev, &st->fifo_buf[i]);`. This assumes the FIFO entry count can be consumed in chunks of `st->fifo_set_size` samples. But the root cause says the device FIFO is populated one sample at a time, so if `fifo_entries` is not a multiple of `st->fifo_set_size`, the final iteration still reads a full `st->fifo_set_size` block, which reads past the actual FIFO contents. There is no guard such as rounding down to a multiple, checking a remainder, or reading one sample at a time. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet in this version.
